title: Same heat on DC
story: A 50 ohm heater element was designed for an AC supply of 10 V peak (a sine wave). You want to test it on the bench, but you only have a 12 V battery. Put a series resistor in the slot so the heater makes the same heat it would make on its AC supply: between 0.95 W and 1.10 W.

goals.label: heater power between 0.95 W and 1.10 W (the same heat as on its AC supply)

hints: On AC the heater sees 10 V peak, which is 10 / sqrt(2) = 7.07 V RMS. Its average power there is 7.07 x 7.07 / 50 = 1 W.
On DC you want 1 W again: the heater needs 7.07 V across it, so the current is 7.07 / 50 = 0.141 A.
The series resistor must drop the remaining 12 - 7.07 = 4.93 V at 0.141 A. Pick the closest part to 4.93 / 0.141 ohm.
